title: QUIC: Handle more than one UDP datagram on a packet
description:
It is possible for a single frame to have more than one
UDP datagram. This can happen with protocols such as MASQUE
(#17502) creating QUIC-in-QUIC tunnels, or with various data
link layers that have more than one IP packet (e.g., DVB-S2
baseband frames, various VSAT acceleration techniques.)

All QUIC packets on a single UDP datagram are processed together,
so the QUIC dissector is only called once per UDP datagram.
That means we can use the current QUIC layer number as a key
into the packet proto data. However, we need to access the proto
data from functions that are called from TLS as well. Add a
function to access the current protocol layer number of a given
proto_id.

Related to #17502

notes.body: @oesh what do you think ? needed for #17502 ?

Yes, this will be needed. A single QUIC packet can carry multiple QUIC datagram frames (with all but the last one having frame type 0x31 and having explicit length; the last frame in the packet can have type 0x30 and save some space). 

Note that there can be multiple encapsulation layers; Apple Private Relay uses 2 layers of encapsulation, other QUIC implementations can use even more. Also, there is the possibility of having QUIC encapsulating H2, which would have HTTP Capsule with another QUIC packet inside, hence the protocol tree can become quite interesting.
@johnthacker What missing for merge this MR ?

I don't think anything is missing, though sample captures would be nice as always. (I have some generated samples that it works on but it would be nice to test on something more real.) 

I just wanted people to review it and it looks like that's done, so I am good with merging it
@johnthacker I will look for captures with multiple 0x31 Datagram frames and will attach here if I find any.
